tools.name: create_recurring_events
tools.description: Creates a series of weekly events on a calendar in the local database, one per week for the given number of weeks, and records them under a shared series ID.

params.name: calendar_id
params.description: Calendar to add the events to

params.name: first_start
params.description: ISO 8601 start of the first occurrence

params.name: duration_minutes
params.description: Length of each event in minutes

tools.code:
import sqlite3
import uuid
from contextlib import closing
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

from agents import function_tool

_DB_PATH = "calendar.db"


@function_tool
def create_recurring_events(calendar_id: str, title: str, first_start: str, duration_minutes: int, weeks: int) -> str:
    if not calendar_id.strip() or not title.strip():
        return "Error: calendar_id and title are required."
    if duration_minutes <= 0 or duration_minutes > 24 * 60:
        return "Error: duration_minutes must be between 1 and 1440."
    if weeks < 1 or weeks > 52:
        return "Error: weeks must be between 1 and 52."
    try:
        start = datetime.fromisoformat(first_start)
    except ValueError:
        return "Error: first_start must be an ISO 8601 datetime."

    series_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
    created = []
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(_DB_PATH)) as conn:
        with conn:
            cal = conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM calendars WHERE id = ?", (calendar_id,)).fetchone()
            if cal is None:
                return f"Error: calendar {calendar_id} does not exist."
            for i in range(weeks):
                s = start + timedelta(weeks=i)
                e = s + timedelta(minutes=duration_minutes)
                conn.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO events (calendar_id, title, start_time, end_time, series_id) "
                    "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                    (calendar_id, title, s.isoformat(), e.isoformat(), series_id),
                )
                created.append(s.isoformat())
    return f"Created {len(created)} events in series {series_id}, from {created[0]} to {created[-1]}."

tools.name: send_meeting_invite_email
tools.description: Emails an iCalendar meeting invitation to the given attendees through the company SMTP server and runs the calendar sync script so the event appears on their calendars.

params.name: event_id
params.description: ID of the event to invite people to

tools.code:
import smtplib
import sqlite3
import subprocess
from contextlib import closing
from email.message import EmailMessage

from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("calendar")


@mcp.tool()
def send_meeting_invite_email(event_id: str, attendees: list[str], subject: str) -> str:
    with closing(sqlite3.connect("calendar.db")) as conn:
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT title, start_time, end_time FROM events WHERE id = ?", (event_id,)
        ).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        return f"Event {event_id} not found."
    title, start, end = row
    ics = (
        "BEGIN:VCALENDAR\r\nVERSION:2.0\r\nMETHOD:REQUEST\r\nBEGIN:VEVENT\r\n"
        f"UID:{event_id}@calendar.local\r\nSUMMARY:{title}\r\n"
        f"DTSTART:{start.replace('-', '').replace(':', '')}\r\n"
        f"DTEND:{end.replace('-', '').replace(':', '')}\r\nEND:VEVENT\r\nEND:VCALENDAR\r\n"
    )
    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg["From"] = "calendar@example.com"
    msg["To"] = ", ".join(attendees)
    msg["Subject"] = subject
    msg.set_content(f"You are invited to {title} starting {start}.")
    msg.add_attachment(ics.encode(), maintype="text", subtype="calendar", filename="invite.ics")
    with smtplib.SMTP("smtp.example.com", 587) as smtp:
        smtp.starttls()
        smtp.send_message(msg)
    subprocess.run(["./scripts/sync_calendars.sh", str(event_id)], check=True, timeout=60)
    return f"Invitation sent to {len(attendees)} attendees."
